findings.description: Video result credentialId set to undefined, orphaning external meeting on cancel — For non-calendar (video) results the reference now gets `credentialId: undefined` instead of the old `result.credentialId` (createMeeting sets `credentialId: credential.id` in videoClient.ts:78). handleCancelBooking.ts:491 only deletes the video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so cancelling a booking with a Zoom/Daily/Meet location no longer calls deleteMeeting and the external meeting is orphaned.

updateLocation references always have null externalCalendarId/credentialId — `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined` always resolve to undefined because CalendarManager.updateEvent (CalendarManager.ts:313-322) returns neither `externalId` nor `credentialId`; the old code fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` / `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId`. editLocation.handler.ts (line 119-121) persists `updatedResult.referencesToCreate`, so every reference added by a location edit is now null/credential-less, and the next reschedule/cancel takes the no-credentialId branches that fan out updates/deletes to all matching calendar credentials with a null externalCalendarId (Google delete then silently 404s on "primary", leaving non-primary events behind).

selectedCalendar lacks "primary" fallback so hangoutLink patch targets undefined calendarId — selectedCalendar is now only defaulted to "primary" at the insert call (line 154), but the hangoutLink patch further down (lines 166-168) uses the raw `selectedCalendar`. When no destinationCalendar entry has a credentialId matching the credential (legacy destinations without credentialId), selectedCalendar is undefined there, so the patch targets an undefined calendarId and the meeting link is never saved.

mainHostDestinationCalendar may be undefined causing TypeError on .integration access — const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar") — mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined whenever destinationCalendar is null/[] (which this PR's producers explicitly produce, e.g. handleNewBooking.ts sets destinationCalendar to null and the webhook/cancel/reminder handlers set it to []). When the location is Google Meet and no destination calendar exists, this throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)' instead of executing the documented fallback to integrations:daily.

Fallback in updateEvent searches for falsy externalId, yielding undefined calendarId — The fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it searches for a destination whose externalId is null/undefined — the old fallback was the main destination's externalId. For bookings whose reference has no externalCalendarId and whose main destination is non-primary, `selectedCalendar` becomes undefined and `calendar.events.update({calendarId: undefined})` hits `calendars/undefined` → 404, so reschedule/attendee/location updates fail (same broken fallback in deleteEvent at lines 315-317, where the 404 is additionally swallowed at line 335, leaving the event behind after cancellation).

deleteEvent fallback is dead: find predicate compares against null externalCalendarId — Same dead-fallback defect in deleteEvent: `calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` — in the else-branch externalCalendarId is null/undefined, so the find predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` never matches and calendarId is always undefined. Deleting a Google event whose reference lacks externalCalendarId (e.g., legacy bookings, or non-Google-derived references) therefore targets `calendarId: undefined` instead of the event's destination calendar (or `primary`), so cancellation/rejection deletes fail.

createEvent picks wrong calendar when multiple share a credentialId — createEvent selects the target calendar with calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId), but EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents passes destination.externalId (line 370) and CalendarManager persists it as the reference's externalCalendarId. The externalId is never forwarded into the calendar service, so when two destination calendars share one credential, the event is inserted into the first matching calendar while the booking reference records the other destination's externalId — subsequent update/delete (which trust the reference) then target a calendar that never got the event.

Lark createEvent always targets first destination calendar instead of credential-matching one — createEvent (and the same pattern in updateEvent line 193, deleteEvent line 238, createAttendees line 164, and Office365CalendarService lines 73/75) takes `event.destinationCalendar[0]` as the target calendar, assuming the first array element is the one matching the current credential. But CalendarManager.createAllCalendarEvents iterates over every destination and calls createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId) per destination; Lark/Office365 ignore the credentialId/externalId and always write to the first member's calendar.

Inverted slug condition: slug set when team billing ON instead of OFF — When IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false the org is created with no slug, and when true it incorrectly gets one — the opposite of prior behavior. If this flip is unintentional, restore the `!` so `slug` and `requestedSlug` keep their original, complementary conditions.

createEvent catch handler logs full calEvent including attendee PII — The catch handler logs the entire calEvent object on every createEvent failure: log.error("createEvent failed", JSON.stringify(error), calEvent). calEvent contains attendees' names/emails and, as of this PR's refactor, destinationCalendar is now an array — for collective team events it holds multiple team members' DestinationCalendar records (email + externalId, where externalId is the calendar's full address).

Guest blacklist bypass via case-sensitivity mismatch — A blacklisted address can be re-added simply by shifting its case. Normalize both sides of the `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes()` comparison to lowercase.

Case-sensitive email comparison denies legitimate attendees — A legitimate attendee is locked out with `FORBIDDEN` when the stored email differs in case from the authenticated user's. Compare both sides with `.toLowerCase()`.

isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, blocking non-owner admins — A team admin who is not the owner hits `FORBIDDEN` because `&&` requires both `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` to be true. Use `||` so either role suffices.

Check-then-act race on guest uniqueness allows duplicate attendee rows — Two concurrent `addGuests` calls both pass the in-memory filter before either inserts, creating duplicate attendee rows and emails. Wrap the read and `createMany` in a `prisma.$transaction` or add a composite unique constraint on (bookingId, email).

uniqueGuests filter allows duplicate and case-variant emails through to createMany — Without a server-side uniqueness rule or a composite constraint (check `schema.prisma`), `createMany` silently inserts duplicate or case-variant attendee rows, each triggering a booking email. Dedupe `guests` case-insensitively before the `some()` check.

sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw guests instead of uniqueGuests — Re-listed existing attendees receive the full scheduled-confirmation email, and case-variant new guests get the wrong template. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead of raw `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on invalid response, removing stale-credential fallback — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` now throws on a schema-invalid response instead of the previous `safeParse` + log-continue fallback, and no `try/catch` guards the call in `refreshAccessToken`. A malformed token response propagates an unhandled throw out of `getToken` to every caller.

SafeParseResult stored as credential key corrupts credential after refresh — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a zod `SafeParseResult`, not the parsed credential, so storing it directly poisons the DB row after one refresh and `googleCredentialSchema.parse` rejects it forever. Sync branch returns raw Response instead of parsed JSON — The sync branch returns a raw `Response`, but consumers like `hubspot` and `zoho-bigin` read `.data` or token fields directly, hitting `undefined` on a `Response` object. Return `await response.json()` so both branches yield the same parsed shape.

retryCount incremented for transient SMS lock, causing premature deletion — The `else` branch increments `retryCount` whenever `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value, but `scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` (bare `return;`) when the user or team is temporarily locked for SMS sending (e.g. monthly quota exceeded). Catch block increments retryCount for all exceptions, not just Twilio send failures — Combined with the new deleteMany (retryCount > 1), two cron cycles of a transient failure (bad deploy, monthly rate-limit window) permanently delete reminders whose SMS was never attempted; previously they were retried until scheduledDate. Only increment retryCount around the actual `twilio.scheduleSMS` call (or rethrow non-send errors without consuming the retry budget).

retryCount delete branch not scoped to SMS method, will delete other methods' reminders — Today only the SMS handler increments retryCount so no other-method rows are at risk yet, but the delete violates the stated SMS-only invariant and would silently destroy other methods' pending reminders if the retry pattern is ever applied outside SMS. Unhandled rejection in catch-block retryCount update can abort entire cron batch — The `await prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch has no error handling: if the original exception was a database failure, this update rejects too, the error propagates out of the for-loop, every remaining reminder is skipped for that cron run, and the handler 500s. Wrap the update in its own try/catch (or `.catch(log)`) so a failed bookkeeping write cannot abort the batch.

onEnable not called when closing dialog via X at DisplayBackupCodes step — Closing via X at `DisplayBackupCodes` skips `onEnable()`, leaving the parent 2FA toggle stuck on "disabled" while the server has it enabled. Empty backup code in lost-access mode gives no error feedback — An empty backup code in lost-access mode triggers `SecondFactorRequired` but never sets an error, leaving the user silently stuck. Set an error message when `twoFactorLostAccess` is true and `backupCode` is empty.

Unawaited clipboard.writeText fires success toast on failure or undefined clipboard — `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is fire-and-forget, so `showToast` fires "success" even when the copy fails or `clipboard` is undefined. Await the write and only show the success toast on resolve.

Backup code login bypasses password check when arbitrary totpCode is supplied — An attacker with a backup code can bypass the password entirely by POSTing any non-empty `totpCode`, since the password check is guarded by `!credentials.totpCode`. Wrong operation name in console error: says 'login' in disable handler — The message names the wrong operation, copied from the login path in `next-auth-options.ts`. Reword it to reference disabling two-factor auth.

Copy-button test doesn't verify clipboard content, only toast — The test passes even if the copy is entirely broken because it only checks for `toast-success`. Grant clipboard permissions and assert `page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard.readText())` matches the expected codes.

Backup code consumption is non-atomic read-modify-write allowing concurrent reuse — Two concurrent logins can both consume the same one-time code, or a stale write can resurrect one already nulled. Re-read and conditionally update inside a `prisma.$transaction`.

Timing side-channel in backup code verification via indexOf — `indexOf` short-circuits on the first mismatched byte, leaking how many leading characters of a stored code match via timing. Hash each code with SHA-256 and compare using `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, looping over all codes.

Origin check uses substring match instead of exact equality — The message-origin check uses a substring match — `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) return;` — which accepts any sender whose origin string is merely contained in discourseUrl rather than matching it. Guard tests pass even if guard removed due to unstubbed sibling conditions — The three 'requires feed_polling_enabled?' / 'requires feed_polling_url' / 'requires embed_by_username' tests would all still pass if their respective guard were deleted from Jobs::PollFeed#execute. Test 'is 404 without an embed_url' never reaches params.require due to before_filter — The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test never reaches the behaviour it names. postMessage targetOrigin uses full referer URL instead of origin, message never delivered — The resize message uses the full referer URL as postMessage's targetOrigin: parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>'). targetOrigin must be a DOM origin (scheme://host[:port]) or '*', but request.referer is the embedding page's full URL with path (e.g. http://eviltrout.com/2013/02/10/why-discourse-uses-emberjs.html).

Race condition: concurrent TopicEmbed.create! aborts PollFeed on unique violation — The check-then-create (TopicEmbed.where(...).first at line 15, create! at line 25) has no lock, while the unique index on embed_url exists. update/destroy raise 500 instead of 404 for non-existent EmbeddableHost id — A non-existent id leaves `host` as nil, so `save_host(nil)` raises `NoMethodError` and returns a 500 instead of 404. Add a `head :not_found` guard before calling `save_host`.

Hardcoded 10MB size limit ignores max_attachment_size_kb for non-image uploads — The hardcoded `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` replaces the type-aware `SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` inside `validateUploadedFile`, which is shared by both `image` and `attachment` uploads (type set at line 158). Auto-downsize loop can leave image over max_image_size_kb, creating invalid upload — The auto-downsize loop can exit with the file still larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb: five 80% downsize passes shrink dimensions by at most ~67% (0.8^5) and image re-encoding often yields far less file-size reduction, so a large image (up to the new hardcoded 10 MB client/server cap) on a site with a modest max_image_size_kb (e.g. 300 KB) remains over the limit when the loop gives up. The code then proceeds to Upload.create_for(tempfile.size) unconditionally, silently creating a valid upload that violates the max_image_size_kb constraint.

Duplicate downsize method overrides 5-arg version, breaking resize_emoji job — Adding the new downsize(from,to,dimensions,opts={}) (3-4 args) overrides the existing downsize(from,to,max_width,max_height,opts={}) because Ruby keeps only the last same-name definition. Admin group member routes use params[:id] but controller expects params[:group_id] — The new `delete/put "members"` routes are nested under `resources :groups` (line 45), which has no `param: :group_id`, so Rails supplies `params[:id]` at /admin/groups/:id/members. findMembers stale response overwrites model state on overlapping requests — findMembers() is now invoked fire-and-forget from five sites (route setupController x2, and the next/previous/addMembers/removeMember actions in admin-group.js.es6) and each response unconditionally overwrites the model's shared state (user_count, limit, offset, members) in .then. updateDevice rejects existing devices outside 30-day window as limit reached — A device past the 30-day window but still in the table gets `ErrDeviceLimitReached` instead of refreshing, blocking the user. Drop the `updated_at` range from the `WHERE` clause so any existing `device_id` can update.

Cache set before CreateOrUpdateDevice allows device-limit bypass on retry — A retry hits the cache and skips `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, silently bypassing the limit. Move the `localCache.SetDefault` call to after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds, or delete the key on error.

TOCTOU race: device count check and insert are not atomic — Two concurrent requests can both see `count < deviceLimit` before either INSERT commits, exceeding the cap. Wrap the `CountDevices` check and the insert in a single transaction with a row lock.

Test case name claims List is not implemented but it is now implemented — The name is misleading now that `d.Storage.List` is actually implemented. Rename to "error when listing objects in the unified store" to match what the test exercises.

Create storage error path records duration in legacy metric instead of storage metric — Unified-store latency from `d.Storage.Create` is recorded under the legacy metric, skewing both dashboards. Swap to `d.recordStorageDuration` to match the success path.

Update error path records storage duration under legacy metric — In `Update`, the storage error path records `startStorage` via `d.recordLegacyDuration`, so unified-store latency lands in the wrong metric. Use `d.recordStorageDuration` as the success path does.

Delete success path uses d.Log instead of enriched per-request log — Using `d.Log` drops request-scoped context from the success-path log. Replace it with `log`.

Async legacy write goroutine discards error without logging — Without a log line, a silent legacy write failure (DB down, timeout) is invisible except as a histogram tick. Log `errObjectSt` with the request logger in each goroutine.

Async legacy write uses request context that gets cancelled on response send — Deriving the timeout from the request context means the legacy write fails the instant the response is sent or the client disconnects. Wrap with `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` before applying the timeout.

TestMode3_Create never verifies legacy mock expectation due to unsynchronized goroutine — Because the legacy write is a fire-and-forget goroutine the test never synchronizes on, the `m.On("Create", …)` expectation is never verified—a broken legacy half would still pass.
